blocks.text: 如何利用智能体团队和形式化验证，改进用于聚变能源、化学与酶建模的量子算法

inlines.text: 如何利用智能体团队和形式化验证，改进用于聚变能源、化学与酶建模的量子算法

blocks.text: 量子计算机或许很快就能解决经典超级计算机力所不及的问题。但有一个前提：即便采用最好的量子算法，一些重要应用所需的资源仍超出早期量子硬件所能支撑的范围。

inlines.text: 量子计算机或许很快就能解决经典超级计算机力所不及的问题。但有一个前提：即便采用最好的量子算法，一些重要应用所需的资源仍超出早期量子硬件所能支撑的范围。

blocks.text: 在一篇新论文中，我们用多支 Gemini 4 智能体团队改进了若干知名量子算法，构建出高效的量子线路。这些优化后的线路规定了量子计算机执行算法的具体方式，未来有望帮助我们运行模拟，攻克从聚变能源到药物设计的复杂科学难题。为方便社区在此基础上继续推进，我们在 GitHub 上开源了我们的 Lean 库、问题规格说明以及经过验证的解法。

、问题规格说明以及经过验证的解法。

blocks.text: 由于无法在经典计算机或当今的小型量子处理器上测试资源密集的量子线路，我们只能从数学上证明其正确性。我们的智能体团队用形式化定理证明器 Lean 逐一证明了每个结果。

inlines.text: 由于无法在经典计算机或当今的小型量子处理器上测试资源密集的量子线路，我们只能从数学上证明其正确性。我们的智能体团队用形式化定理证明器 Lean 逐一证明了每个结果。

blocks.text: 用智能体团队改进量子算法 针对每个问题，我们安排彼此独立的多支智能体团队分头寻找算法改进。这些想法先经 Lean 验证，再进入共享笔记库。每四小时，各团队的智能体在虚拟会议上碰面，交换、辩论并比较想法。随着团队不断产出更有效的思路，计算成本逐步下降，直至实验结束。

inlines.text: 用智能体团队改进量子算法
针对每个问题，我们安排彼此独立的多支智能体团队分头寻找算法改进。这些想法先经 Lean 验证，再进入共享笔记库。每四小时，各团队的智能体在虚拟会议上碰面，交换、辩论并比较想法。随着团队不断产出更有效的思路，计算成本逐步下降，直至实验结束。

blocks.text: 我们选择聚焦于有朝一日可能影响人类重大挑战的应用，例如清洁能源和药物设计，但我们的方法并不局限于这些领域。

inlines.text: 我们选择聚焦于有朝一日可能影响人类重大挑战的应用，例如清洁能源和药物设计，但我们的方法并不局限于这些领域。
我们找到了一种量子线路，有助于计算惯性约束聚变的一项关键性质。惯性约束聚变是一种用激光压缩氢燃料直至点火的聚变方式。我们的智能体团队将所需计算成本（一项综合所需量子比特数与操作数的指标）降低了 11.8 倍，并将所需内存从 5,650 个
纠错量子比特
智能体还降低了药物代谢中分子模拟以及某些光化学反应模拟的成本，后者是经典计算机难以模拟的复杂反应。对于一种常见的光敏分子，智能体团队让量子模拟成本降低 8 倍，简化了算法追踪粒子位置与电场力的方式。对于细胞色素 P450——一种能分解大多数人类药物、对药物设计至关重要的酶——他们通过替换笨重的内存查表，实现了 2.5 倍的改进，并将所需内存从 481 个量子比特降至 333 个。
我们还改进了一个基础量子算法和一个广泛使用的算术构件。针对 Grover 算法的一种特定实现，我们实现了 2.57 倍加速；Grover 算法是在无序列表中搜索的基础量子操作。对于 arcsin，我们实现了 290 倍加速；arcsin 是一种常用例程，许多其他量子算法用它把数值加载到量子态中。

blocks.text: 在科学模拟中运行这些算法，所需计算资源仍会超过首批纠错量子计算机可能提供的水平，但这些改进意义重大。

inlines.text: 在科学模拟中运行这些算法，所需计算资源仍会超过首批纠错量子计算机可能提供的水平，但这些改进意义重大。

blocks.text: 我们找到它们的方式同样令人兴奋。我们构建了一个新的开源库，用 Lean 编写，面向量子算法，可供协作智能体团队使用，因此它们的想法有数学正确性保证作为支撑。随后，我们可以通过为智能体团队指定问题来设定研究方向，并监督它们的进展。我们对量子算法的了解，加上我们组建智能体团队的方式，带来了真正的科学成果。

blocks.text: How using agent teams and formal verification can improve quantum algorithms for modelling fusion energy, chemistry and enzymes

inlines.text: How using agent teams and formal verification can improve quantum algorithms for modelling fusion energy, chemistry and enzymes

blocks.text: Quantum computers could soon solve problems beyond the reach of classical supercomputers. However, there is a catch: even when using the best quantum algorithms, some important applications still require more resources than early quantum hardware will be able to support.

inlines.text: Quantum computers could soon solve problems beyond the reach of classical supercomputers. However, there is a catch: even when using the best quantum algorithms, some important applications still require more resources than early quantum hardware will be able to support.

blocks.text: In a new paper, we used teams of Gemini 4 agents to improve well-known quantum algorithms, creating highly efficient quantum circuits. These optimized circuits, which are instructions for how a quantum computer should carry out an algorithm, could one day help us run simulations that solve complex scientific challenges, from fusion energy to drug design. To help the community build on this work, we are open-sourcing our Lean library, problem specifications, and verified solutions on GitHub.

new paper

, we used teams of Gemini 4 agents to improve well-known quantum algorithms, creating highly efficient quantum circuits. These optimized circuits, which are instructions for how a quantum computer should carry out an algorithm, could one day help us run simulations that solve complex scientific challenges, from fusion energy to drug design. To help the community build on this work, we are open-sourcing

blocks.text: Because we cannot test resource-intensive quantum circuits on classical computers or today's small quantum processors, we have to prove that they work mathematically. Our agent teams proved each result using Lean, a formal theorem prover.

inlines.text: Because we cannot test resource-intensive quantum circuits on classical computers or today's small quantum processors, we have to prove that they work mathematically. Our agent teams proved each result using Lean, a formal theorem prover.

blocks.text: Improving quantum algorithms using agentic teams For each problem, we tasked separate, independent agent teams with finding algorithmic improvements. These ideas were then verified with Lean, before entering a shared notebook. Every four hours, agents from each team met at a virtual conference to trade, debate and compare ideas. As teams produced more effective ideas over time, the computational cost gradually fell until the experiment finished.

inlines.text: Improving quantum algorithms using agentic teams

For each problem, we tasked separate, independent agent teams with finding algorithmic improvements. These ideas were then verified with Lean, before entering a shared notebook. Every four hours, agents from each team met at a virtual conference to trade, debate and compare ideas. As teams produced more effective ideas over time, the computational cost gradually fell until the experiment finished.

blocks.text: We chose to focus on applications that could one day impact some of humanity’s greatest challenges, such as clean energy and drug design, but our method is not limited to these problem areas.

inlines.text: We chose to focus on applications that could one day impact some of humanity’s greatest challenges, such as clean energy and drug design, but our method is not limited to these problem areas.

We found a quantum circuit that helps calculate an important property of inertial confinement fusion, a fusion reaction method that uses lasers to compress hydrogen fuel until ignition. Our agent teams cut the required computing cost (a metric that combines required qubits and operations) by 11.8×, and lowered required memory from 5,650 to 4,338
error-corrected qubits

The agents also reduced costs for simulating molecules in drug metabolism and certain photochemical reactions, which are complex reactions that are difficult for classical computers to simulate. For a common light-sensitive molecule, the agent teams made quantum simulation 8× cheaper, simplifying how the algorithm tracks particle positions and electric forces. For Cytochrome P450, an enzyme that breaks down most human medicines and is important for drug design, they found a 2.5× improvement and lowered memory from 481 to 333 qubits, by replacing bulky memory lookups.

We also improved a fundamental quantum algorithm and a widely used arithmetic building block. We found a 2.57x speedup for a specific implementation of Grover's algorithm, a foundational quantum operation that searches through an unsorted list, and a 290x speedup for arcsin, a common routine that is used by many other quantum algorithms to load numbers into quantum states.

blocks.text: Running these algorithms in scientific simulations would still demand more computational resources than the first error-corrected quantum computers are likely to provide, but these improvements are significant.

inlines.text: Running these algorithms in scientific simulations would still demand more computational resources than the first error-corrected quantum computers are likely to provide, but these improvements are significant.

blocks.text: We are also excited by the way in which we found them. We built a new, open-source library, in Lean for quantum algorithms which could be used by teams of collaborating agents, so their ideas were backed by mathematical correctness guarantees. We could then set the research direction by specifying the problems for our agent teams and supervise their progress. Our knowledge of quantum algorithms, combined with the way we set up our agent teams, led to real scientific results.

blocks.text: The same approach could also accelerate other aspects of quantum computing research, and scientific discovery more broadly. Proof-checked AI search compresses work that once took years of manual design, empowering researchers to focus on choosing problems and interpreting results.
